All integer, bit-exact vs a C golden model (score and id); 7.993 sustained / 8.000 peak dims/clock (P=8 roofline), 1-cycle fill/drain latency; 21.80x aggregate / 25.00x peak over a documented scalar cost-model baseline; 49 searches / 7364 vectors / 58912 beats per pass (9 directed corner cases - single vector, exactly-K, fewer-than-K, planted zero-distance hit, all-identical ties, IP argmax, IP ties, int8 saturation extremes - plus 40 randomised) checked bit-exact under randomised ingress bubbles and again at full rate, 762 result entries/pass, plus CSR statistics, a truncated-shard error/IRQ directed test, and full differential sim at D/P/K = 64/8/8, 32/4/4, 128/16/16, 256/16/8, 0 mismatches.

projects.name: gpu_kv_cache_paging_engine
projects.domain: memory management / paged KV-cache address translation for LLM serving (heterogeneous inference)
projects.microarchitecture: set-associative translation cache (SETS x WAYS parallel tag compare, true-LRU move-to-front order vector, invalid-way-first victim) + a block-table walker FSM + a LIFO physical-block allocator with a combinational stack-top read, all advancing on one bus-done gate so memory wait states stall the walk losslessly; the walker presents the next translation's key to the cache probe port while the current result word is on the bus, retiring one translation per bus transaction
projects.interface: Wishbone B4 classic single master over shared system memory (request array fetch, block-table read/write, result array writeback) + MMIO control/status register file with pool seeding, seven paging statistics counters and a sticky done / out-of-memory / bus-error interrupt cleared W1C
projects.software_layer: bare-metal C driver (configure, seed the block pool, submit a batch, wait on the interrupt, read paging statistics), a bit-exact golden model of the cache/LRU/allocator/block-table, a serving-trace workload generator, and a documented scalar cost-model baseline
projects.verification: Icarus Verilog SystemVerilog differential testbench with a Wishbone B4 slave memory model: two full passes over a 16-batch serving trace (randomised 0-3 memory wait states, then zero wait states) checking every result word (physical block AND flags), all seven statistics CSRs, FREE_COUNT/RES_WORDS, the sticky OOM bit and the IRQ, plus the entire 2048-word block table against the golden image; directed Wishbone ERR_I and never-acknowledged (watchdog) bus-error tests; mutation-checked (broken LRU victim and FIFO-instead-of-LIFO pool both fail); full differential simulation at 16x4/512, 8x2/256, 32x8/512 and 4x4/64 geometries
projects.summary: GPU/heterogeneous-inference KV-cache paging engine - the paged-attention (vLLM PagedAttention) block-table front end of an LLM serving stack: the attention kernels want physical KV-block numbers, the runtime thinks in (sequence, logical block) pairs, and this engine translates at bus rate while owning block allocation and release. A set-associative translation cache resolves a translation in one cycle (WAYS parallel tag compares, true-LRU move-to-front replacement, invalid-way-first victim); on a miss a block-table walker reads block_table[seq][idx] over Wishbone B4, fills the cache on a valid entry, and on an unmapped entry pops a physical block from a LIFO allocator, writes the entry back and reports ALLOC; OP_FREE walks a sequence's row, pushes each block back, invalidates its cache entry and poisons the entry, so the next allocation reuses blocks in LIFO order; OP_NOALLOC probes without growing, OP_FLUSH invalidates the cache, and an exhausted pool raises a sticky out-of-memory interrupt instead of evicting on its own (policy stays in software). Every state advances only on the bus-done gate, so wait states stretch the walk without changing a result, and the walker absorbs the next translation's key while the current result word is on the bus - 0.970 translations/clock peak (93.5% Wishbone occupancy), 3-cycle single-translation latency, 0.384 sustained translations/clock, 13.02x aggregate / 20.42x peak over a documented scalar cost-model baseline. Bit-exact against a C golden model over 16 batches / 371 request words / 1909 translations / 1955 result words per pass (directed: cold prefill, fully-cached re-read, flush-and-rewalk, NOALLOC on mapped and unmapped blocks, eviction + LIFO reuse, pool exhaustion mid-range, unknown opcode, both zero-count forms, host-populated rows, 9-way LRU thrash on one 4-way set, a 512-translation peak batch, plus 320 randomised requests) checked under randomised memory wait states and again at full rate, 8464 checks, including the whole 2048-word block table, plus CSR statistics, an out-of-memory IRQ, Wishbone ERR_I and bus-watchdog directed tests, and full differential simulation at 16x4/512, 8x2/256, 32x8/512, 4x4/64, 0 mismatches.

projects.name: gpu_embedding_gather_engine
projects.domain: recommendation inference / sharded embedding-table gather-reduce (DLRM / TorchRec multi-GPU EmbeddingBag)
projects.microarchitecture: double-buffered (ping-pong) row-staging pipeline: two CHUNKS x LANES x 32 staging buffers so the CHUNKS-beat memory burst of row i+1 overlaps the CHUNKS-cycle pooling fold of row i exactly, feeding LANES one-adder-deep reduce lanes (32-bit wrapping add for SUM/MEAN, signed compare-select for MAX/MIN, first-row init instead of a sentinel) into a CHUNKS-deep accumulator, with a divide-in-place MEAN pass through LANES 34-stage pipelined restoring dividers that needs no drain FIFO; CTRL.SINGLE_BUF collapses the overlap for a same-RTL A/B measurement
projects.interface: AXI4 burst read master (descriptor fetch, bag-index fetch, row gather; ARSIZE = LANES*4 bytes, INCR, AR beat presented the cycle the request is accepted) + AXI4 burst write master (pooled-vector scatter, W beats allowed to lag AW so the MEAN divider pass runs first) over shared device memory, driven by a host-built 8-word descriptor ring, plus a 19-register MMIO control/status plane carrying the shard window, seven pooling statistics counters and a sticky done / baglen / index / bus-error interrupt cleared W1C
projects.software_layer: bare-metal C firmware (descriptor-ring build from a batch of sparse features, shard-window and geometry configuration, device-ID bitstream check, start, interrupt service with W1C acknowledge, statistics readback for all-to-all sizing, and a host-side self-check), a bit-exact golden model of the classify/gather/pool/renormalise semantics, a workload generator, and a documented scalar cost-model baseline
projects.verification: Icarus Verilog SystemVerilog differential testbench with an AXI4 slave memory model: four full passes over a 319-bag ring (randomised 0-3 wait states on all five AXI channels, full rate, single-buffer mode, and a post-fault recovery run) checking every one of 20416 pooled output words against the golden image plus all seven statistics CSRs cross-checked against the beats the slave actually saw; the entire 41792-word descriptor/index/table region is compared against the pre-run image to prove the engine writes nothing outside the output region, and the output region is poisoned with 0xDEADC0DE so a missing write is a mismatch; 19 directed descriptors (empty bag, single local, single remote, all-remote, exactly LANES indices, MAX over INT32_MIN and -1, MIN over INT32_MAX and -1, SUM wrapping at INT32_MAX, MEAN truncating toward zero at -7/2, MEAN with count 1, MEAN exact, MEAN over alternating INT32_MAX/INT32_MIN, duplicate index five times, both shard boundaries, shard_hi classified remote, MAX_BAG-deep peak bag, num_idx > MAX_BAG rejection, index >= TABLE_ROWS, local+remote+invalid mixture) plus 300 randomised bags; directed read-SLVERR, AR-watchdog and zero-length-ring tests plus IRQ assert/W1C checks; mutation-checked (dropping the first-row accumulator init and renormalising MEAN by bag length instead of local count both fail); full differential simulation at EMB_DIM/LANES/MAX_BAG = 64/4/64, 32/8/32, 128/4/48, 32/2/64, 928256 checks, 0 mismatches
projects.summary: GPU/heterogeneous-inference sharded embedding gather-reduce engine - the nn.EmbeddingBag lookup path of a multi-GPU recommender (DLRM / TorchRec), where the sparse tower and not the dense one is the latency floor. Given a host-built ring of 8-word descriptors, each one a bag of row indices plus a pooling op, the engine fetches the descriptor, fetches the whole bag into a MAX_BAG-deep index buffer so the row gather never interleaves pointer loads with data loads, then classifies every index against this device's shard window [SHARD_LO, SHARD_HI): a local hit becomes one CHUNKS-beat AXI4 INCR burst, an index owned by a peer shard is skipped and counted in ST_REMOTE (which is what sizes the all-to-all that follows, so it is not an error), and only an index past the end of the global table raises a sticky error. The datapath is double buffered: row i+1 streams into one staging buffer while LANES one-adder-deep reduce lanes fold row i out of the other, one beat per clock, and because a row takes CHUNKS cycles to fold and CHUNKS beats to fetch the two stages are exactly matched - CTRL.SINGLE_BUF collapses the overlap in the same RTL and measures the gain at 1.667x. MEAN renormalises by the locally pooled count through LANES 34-stage pipelined restoring dividers writing quotients back in place, truncating toward zero exactly like C's /, so no drain FIFO is needed; an all-remote bag pools nothing and emits the zero vector the sharded reduce expects, and MAX/MIN are correct with no sentinel because the first locally pooled row initialises the accumulator. Every result is a function of the descriptor ring alone, never of bus timing or the buffering mode - 3.374 pooled words/clock peak (87.1% AXI occupancy, 18.97 cycles per 16-beat row), 2.917 sustained, 1.667x from double buffering, 13.17x aggregate / 14.08x peak over a documented scalar cost-model baseline. Bit-exact against a C golden model over 319 bags / 9523 indices / 6000 gathered rows / 384000 pooled embedding words / 20416 output words per pass (19 directed corner cases - empty bag, single local, single remote, all-remote, exactly LANES indices, MAX over INT32_MIN and -1, MIN over INT32_MAX and -1, SUM wrapping at INT32_MAX, MEAN truncating toward zero, MEAN count 1, MEAN exact, MEAN over alternating extremes, duplicate index five times, both shard boundaries, shard_hi as remote, a MAX_BAG-deep peak bag, num_idx > MAX_BAG rejection, index >= TABLE_ROWS, and a local+remote+invalid mixture - plus 300 randomised bags) checked under randomised AXI wait states, at full rate, in single-buffer mode and again after injected faults, 248960 checks per pass, including proof that nothing outside the output region is written, CSR statistics cross-checked against real bus beats, read-SLVERR / AR-watchdog / zero-length-ring / IRQ W1C directed tests, mutation checks, and full differential simulation at 64/4/64, 32/8/32, 128/4/48, 32/2/64, 928256 checks, 0 mismatches.

projects.name: gpu_kernel_dag_scheduler
projects.domain: heterogeneous runtime / multi-GPU kernel-DAG launch scheduling (CUDA-Graph command processor for heterogeneous inference)
projects.microarchitecture: associative dependency scoreboard: an on-chip graph CAM holding MAX_NODES x {dependency bitmask, device-affinity mask, duration, kernel id} whose masks are read out in parallel every tick, so all MAX_NODES readiness matches ((dep & ~done) == 0) resolve in one cycle; a combinational placer ANDs each ready node's affinity with the free-device mask and picks the winner through a two-level (group-of-8) priority encoder plus a device encoder, with fixed lowest-index tie-breaks; DEVICES countdown execution slots retire independently and in parallel, the retirement being registered so the done bit and the freed slot appear together on the next tick; the RUN phase touches no bus at all, so the schedule is a pure function of the graph, and nothing-runnable-with-nothing-running is an exact cycle detection rather than a timeout
projects.interface: AXI4-Lite control slave (18-register control/status plane: doorbell, node count, node/result base addresses, seven scheduling statistics counters, per-device occupancy, CAPS, and a sticky graph-done / error interrupt cleared W1C) plus a pipelined AXI4-Lite memory master (up to 4 outstanding addresses, AR running ahead of R, in-order returns so no reorder buffer is needed; AW and W held until both handshake, completion on B) reading a host-built node array and scattering one 4-word result record per kernel node
projects.software_layer: bare-metal C driver (graph construction in shared memory with an edge helper, device-affinity policy, launch doorbell, interrupt service with W1C acknowledge, per-node schedule readback and CSR collection, parallel-efficiency reporting for the next launch's rebalancing) plus a tick-by-tick golden model of the RUN phase and a software-only scheduler baseline that charges the CPU for every readiness scan visit, completion poll, launch and graph word load
projects.verification: 326 graph launches per pass (17 directed shapes + 9 directed rejection cases + 300 randomised DAGs generated in topological order then relabelled with a random permutation), 9991 kernel nodes, checked bit-exact against a C golden model on the per-node schedule and every CSR under randomised wait states on all five AXI4-Lite memory channels and again at full rate, 255388 checks per pass including a full 80844-word memory sweep proving nothing outside a result region is written, the two structural identities (makespan == dispatched + stall + depwait, sum(dev_busy) == serial_ticks), read/write SLVERR, fault recovery, IRQ masking and W1C tests, mutation-checked with three injected defects, and full differential simulation at 64x4, 32x2, 32x8 and 128x4 - 1113064 checks, 0 mismatches
projects.summary: A hardware command processor that launches a CUDA-Graph-shaped DAG of kernels onto the GPUs of a node by itself: an associative dependency scoreboard answers 'which kernels are runnable now' for all MAX_NODES at once, a combinational placer picks the lowest ready node and the lowest idle device its affinity mask allows, and DEVICES countdown slots retire in parallel so a dependent issues the cycle its last predecessor retires. 0.985 nodes/clock peak dispatch, 32-cycle single-graph latency, 2.583x parallel compression of 146263 serial ticks into 56632, 98.4% AXI4-Lite occupancy in the transfer phases, 17.62x aggregate / 18.37x peak over a documented scalar cost-model baseline.

projects.name: gpu_p2p_transport_engine
projects.domain: networking / GPU-to-GPU peer interconnect transport (RDMA-style link for tensor-parallel inference collectives)
projects.microarchitecture: credit-based streaming dataflow across two decoupled pipelines: a transmit segmentation engine that turns a work-queue entry into MTU-sized packets (two header beats + payload) and prefetches payload into an 8-deep staging FIFO starting on the header beats, so the memory round trip is hidden inside the packet rather than added to it; a store-and-forward receiver whose RX_BUFS x MTU_WORDS packet buffer pool *is* the credit pool, with in-order slot allocation and release so commits reach memory in arrival order; per-queue-pair 8-bit sequence numbers with whole-packet discard and resynchronisation on a gap; a receive-side accumulate fold (dst += payload, 32-bit wrapping) pipelined behind an 8-deep result FIFO so destination reads run ahead of writes, gated at packet boundaries on the write pipeline being drained; and a round-robin arbiter with a grant-order tag FIFO sharing one AXI4-Lite read channel between descriptor fetch, transmit payload fetch and the accumulate fold, with the write channel owned by the receive path alone so a full-duplex transfer moves one word out of memory and one word in on the same clock
projects.interface: shared work-queue / completion-queue rings in memory (8-word descriptors, 4-word completions) driven by an AXI4-Lite control slave (24-register control/status plane: doorbell, ring bases, MEM_LIMIT range guard, CREDIT_LIM, sequence-gap injection, eleven statistics counters including credit-stall / link-stall / memory-stall counted separately, CAPS, and a sticky done / error interrupt cleared W1C) plus a pipelined AXI4-Lite memory master (separate 4-outstanding read and write channels), a 32-bit AXI4-Stream egress and ingress link pair (TLAST per packet, TUSER marking the header beat) and a per-queue-pair credit-return sideband
projects.software_layer: bare-metal C driver (ring construction, queue-pair assignment, doorbell, interrupt service with W1C acknowledge, completion-ring reaping, and a policy routine that reads the three stall counters and reports whether the peer needs more receive buffers, the wire is saturated, or the engine is contending with compute for memory bandwidth) plus a message-level golden model of a launch and a documented scalar cost-model baseline that charges the CPU for every descriptor load, validation, header build, packet post, flow-control test, payload word in each direction and completion store
projects.verification: 331 launches per pass (31 directed cases + 300 randomised), replayed three times - under randomised wait states on all five AXI4-Lite memory channels with randomised link backpressure and credit-return delay, at full rate, and again with every launch forced down to a single credit - all three required to produce byte-identical memory and identical counters; 2283 packets and 28328 payload words per pass; 221952 checks per pass set including a full 70656-word memory sweep proving nothing outside a destination region, completion slot or message extent is written; directed control-plane tests for CAPS, a register-map checksum cross-checking sw/p2p.h against rtl/p2p_defs.vh, an unmapped register, CREDIT_LIM clamping, interrupt masking, W1C, read SLVERR on a descriptor fetch, write SLVERR on a payload commit, and post-fault recovery; mutation-checked with four injected defects, all caught; full differential simulation at MTU/QP/RX_BUFS of 16/4/4, 32/2/4, 8/8/8 and 64/4/2 - 890883 checks, 0 mismatches
projects.summary: The interconnect layer under a multi-GPU collective: an RDMA-style transport engine that drains a work-queue ring, segments each message into MTU-sized packets, moves them over an AXI4-Stream link under credit-based flow control, and reassembles, commits and completes them at the far end - optionally folding the payload into the destination instead of overwriting it, which is a reduce-scatter done on the wire with no kernel launched on the receiving device. A credit is a receive buffer, so nothing is ever dropped and there is no retransmit path; slots are allocated and freed in order, so the memory image is a function of the descriptor ring and not of bus, wire or flow-control timing. 0.788 payload words/clock peak (88.6% link occupancy against a 0.889 roofline set by the two header beats per 16-word packet), 0.451 words/clock with the accumulate fold, 29-cycle single-word message latency, 10.30x aggregate / 15.01x peak over a documented scalar cost-model baseline.

projects.name: gpu_spec_decode_verifier
projects.domain: LLM serving / tree-based speculative decoding draft-tree verification (the acceptance step between a draft device and the target GPU)
projects.microarchitecture: broadcast-compare node array with a log-depth argmax reduction: the whole draft tree is held in MAX_NODES x 112 flops rather than a RAM, because every node has to be interrogated on every step of the walk - on each step all N nodes simultaneously answer 'is my parent the node being extended, and does my token pass the acceptance predicate', producing a candidate mask cand[j] = live(j) & (par[j] == cur) & accept(j) that a ceil(log2(N))-level argmax tree reduces to a winner in the same cycle, so an accepted token costs one clock whatever the fan-out; ties break to the lowest index structurally (the merge takes the right child only when valid AND strictly greater, and leaf i is seeded with index i) rather than by a comparison, which makes the selected path a pure function of the tree and not of node numbering; the per-node typical-acceptance floor thr[j] = max(TH_ABS, (pmax[j] * TH_REL) >> 16) is precomputed by one 16x16 multiplier as the nodes arrive, so the walk's critical path is broadcast mux -> compare -> argmax tree with no multiplier in it; structural validation is three parallel reductions over the same array, priority-encoded NNODES > ROOT > PARENT > SELF, so checking an N-node tree is one cycle; the walk pushes the node selected in cycle k during cycle k+1, keeping the winner mux out of the selection path, and CHECK gates on the result FIFO being empty so a job that has started stepping can never be stalled by egress backpressure
projects.interface: APB3 control slave (21-register control/status plane: CTRL with EN / IRQ_EN / 2-bit acceptance MODE / self-clearing CLR_STAT and SOFT_RST, TH_ABS and TH_REL acceptance thresholds in Q0.16, MAX_ACC clamped to MAX_DEPTH in hardware, STATUS, sticky IRQ_STAT with DONE/ERROR/CLAMP cleared write-1-to-clear, latched ERRCODE, CAPS, VERSION, ten statistics counters including separate source-starve and backpressure stall counts, a REGMAP_CSUM that cross-checks rtl/sdv_defs.vh against sw/sdv.h, and MAX_DEPTH HIST[k] per-position acceptance counters; PREADY tied high, PSLVERR on unmapped addresses) + 128-bit AXI4-Stream ingress carrying one draft-tree node record per beat {parent, draft token, target argmax, score, pmax} with TLAST ending the tree + 128-bit AXI4-Stream egress carrying accepted-token beats then a trailer beat with TLAST {accepted count, bonus token, error code, (nodes << 16) | flags}; the job configuration is latched on the first ingress beat rather than on a doorbell, so there is no doorbell write in the steady-state path at all
projects.software_layer: bare-metal C firmware (sw/sdv_driver.c): probe against VERSION and the register-map checksum, arm the acceptance policy for the next decode step in four register writes that are safe to issue while the previous step is still draining, consume the egress beats into accepted tokens and node indices (which is what tells the runtime which KV-cache rows to keep), acknowledge the interrupt W1C, and two telemetry routines that turn the counters into decisions - one reads the per-position histogram and returns the depth beyond which fewer than one step in eight is still being accepted, i.e. the depth the draft tree should be truncated to, the other splits busy cycles into draft-link starvation versus egress backpressure. Plus a bit-exact golden model (sw/sdv_model.c) that mirrors the hardware's order of operations, and an independently written scalar baseline (sw/sdv_baseline.c) with a documented cycle cost model; the stimulus generator refuses to emit vectors unless model and baseline agree on every beat
projects.verification: 333 jobs per pass (33 directed + 300 randomised), replayed five ways: pass A one job at a time under randomised 30% ingress bubbles and 35% egress backpressure, pass B the same jobs back to back at full rate with ingress and egress concurrent, pass C the peak and minimum jobs alone with the measured cycle count checked against nodes + accepted + 3, pass D the control plane (VERSION, CAPS, register-map checksum against sw/sdv.h, all five cumulative counters and all MAX_DEPTH histogram buckets against the model's totals, PSLVERR on two unmapped addresses and its absence on a mapped one, IRQ masking, stickiness, W1C acknowledge and the latched error code), pass E soft reset then a job to prove recovery. Passes A and B must produce identical beats and identical counters, so no result may depend on link timing. Directed cases include a three-way score tie where the lowest index must win, the highest score winning from the last index, typical mode exactly on the threshold and one below, the relative threshold dominating the absolute, pmax = 0, both thresholds zero, saturated 0xFFFF probabilities, BOTH and ANY mode corners, reverse labelling where every parent has a higher index than its child, an unreachable 2-cycle beside a live chain (inert, not an error), duplicate sibling tokens separated only by score, MAX_ACC of 0, of 1 and above MAX_DEPTH, and 9 rejection cases (too many nodes, exactly one node past the array, node 0 not a root, a second root, a dangling parent, a self edge, three checks failing at once, PARENT outranking SELF, and a good job after the bad ones). The randomised trees are built parent-before-child then relabelled through a random permutation fixing node 0, so index order is deliberately not tree order. 10772 checks per pass, 0 mismatches; mutation-checked with six injected defects all caught (argmax tie-break to the high index, threshold taking the min, acceptance compare losing its equal case, MAX_ACC not clamped to MAX_DEPTH, error priority reordered, over-length detector off by one beat); full differential simulation at MAX_NODES x MAX_DEPTH of 64x16, 128x16, 32x8, 64x4 and 16x4 - 48156 checks, 0 mismatches; sanitizer gate (UBSan + ASan, -fno-sanitize-recover=all) clean over every generated vector
projects.summary: The acceptance step of tree-based speculative decoding, in hardware. A draft model proposes a tree of continuations and the target model verifies them in one forward pass; the part in between - finding the longest acceptable path through that tree - is a pointer chase the host CPU does while both GPUs sit idle, O(nodes x depth) comparisons with a data-dependent branch per iteration and no index from a parent to its children. Here the tree is loaded into an on-chip flop array and every step of the walk tests all 64 nodes at once, with a 6-level argmax tree naming the winner in the same cycle, so an accepted token costs one clock whatever the fan-out and the cost grows with nodes + depth instead of nodes x depth. Four acceptance modes (greedy against the target's argmax, typical against max(TH_ABS, pmax * TH_REL), both, either), a software cap on the accepted path that the hardware clamps to MAX_DEPTH itself and flags when it bites, structural validation of the whole tree in one cycle with a fixed error priority, and a per-position acceptance histogram counted free on the datapath - which is the measurement that tells a serving runtime whether its draft tree should be deeper or wider, and the one the firmware turns into exactly that recommendation. The policy is latched on the first ingress beat rather than on a doorbell, so the host programs the next step while the current one drains and there is no doorbell write in the steady-state path. 0.941 accepted tokens/clock through the walk against a 1.000 roofline, 1.000 nodes/clock during load, 4-cycle minimum job latency, 10.44x aggregate / 12.74x against engine-busy cycles / 22.55x peak over a documented scalar cost model that charges the CPU for every node it examines. Bit-exact against a C golden model - itself cross-checked against an independent scalar baseline before any vector is emitted - over 333 jobs / 10654 nodes / 1050 egress beats per pass, 10772 checks, 0 mismatches, under randomised ingress bubbles and egress backpressure and again at full rate with identical counters; mutation-checked with six injected defects all caught, five-geometry differential sweep at 48156 checks, 0 mismatches.

projects.name: gpu_mx_cast_riscv_unit
projects.domain: compression / block-scaled numeric format conversion (OCP Microscaling MXFP4 cast kernels for quantised LLM inference and inter-device tensor transfer)
projects.microarchitecture: custom functional unit tightly coupled to a three-stage RV32I pipeline (F / X / W, one retire per cycle): five combinational stateless custom-0 instructions sit in the execute stage beside the ALU, two bf16 elements per instruction because a 32-bit register holds exactly two, so the unit's width is set by the register file rather than chosen. MXQ4 is the longest path - exponent subtract, one variable shift with a sticky OR of everything shifted out, then seven midpoint magnitude comparisons in parallel feeding a 3-bit population count, which is precisely the sequence a scalar machine has to serialise. Round-to-nearest-even on the non-uniform E2M1 grid {0,.5,1,1.5,2,3,4,6} needs no tie detection and no table: the pair straddling midpoint k is (k,k+1), so the even member is k for even k and k+1 for odd k, which is exactly the difference between a strict and a non-strict compare, and adding the sticky bit to the operand expresses 'strictly above the midpoint' without a second comparison. Pipeline hazards resolve through a single W-to-X bypass that also covers load-use, so there is no load-use stall and the only bubble in the machine is the one instruction fetched behind a taken branch - making cycles = instructions retired + taken branches + 2 an exact identity the testbench checks on every job. Traps are precise and priority-encoded WDOG > FETCH > ILLEGAL > ALIGN > RANGE; a trapping instruction does not retire, write a register or touch memory. Both single-ported SRAMs are owned by the core while it runs and by the host while it is halted, by contract rather than by arbitration.
projects.interface: MMIO register file over a selected/ready host bus with one wait state (22 registers at 0x0_0000: CTRL with self-clearing START / SOFT_RST / CLR_STAT and a sticky IRQ_EN, STATUS, sticky IRQ_STAT with DONE/TRAP cleared write-1-to-clear, latched ERRCODE and TRAP_PC, START_PC, WDOG as a retired-instruction budget, six performance counters - CYCLES, INSTRET, CUSTOM_OPS, BRANCH_TAKEN, LOADS, STORES - ARG0..ARG3 loaded into a0..a3 at launch, RETVAL read back from a0 at the halt, HALT_PC, CAPS carrying both memory widths and the custom-instruction count, VERSION, and a REGMAP_CSUM that cross-checks rtl/mxq_defs.vh against sw/mxq.h) plus an instruction-memory window at 0x1_0000 and a data-memory window at 0x2_0000, both accessible only while the core is halted, and a completion/trap interrupt
projects.software_layer: sw/mxq.h shared register map and format constants; sw/mxq_model.c the Q4.8 fixed-point definition of the cast; sw/mxq_baseline.c an independent floating-point implementation that picks the nearest grid value by absolute distance (checked against the model over all 65536 bf16 values at 11 scales before any vector is emitted) plus a scalar cost model; sw/mxq_asm.c an RV32I instruction emitter and sw/mxq_asm.h its readable names, since there is no toolchain in the loop and the custom opcodes would need one patched anyway; sw/mxq_kernels.c four cast kernels - quantise and dequantise, each once with custom-0 and once in strictly base RV32I, emitted from the same file so the two versions are visibly the same algorithm - plus a 33-result ISA conformance program and seven trap programs; sw/mxq_iss.c an instruction-set simulator that emits the commit trace the testbench compares against; sw/mxq_host.c the vector generator; sw/mxq_driver.c the host driver (probe, program load, run, counter report, strerror)
projects.verification: Every job runs twice - once with randomised gaps on the host bus and a randomised delay before the interrupt is serviced, once at full rate - and both passes must produce identical memory, identical counters and an identical commit trace. Per job the testbench checks the commit trace instruction by instruction against the simulator (PC, destination register, value written, memory address, store data of every architectural write, in order), the contents of data memory including a 16-word poison guard band either side of every destination, and all six counters plus the trap cause, trap PC, halt PC, return value and IRQ_STAT; per pass it sweeps the entire 4096-word data memory against a shadow it maintains itself. 1561 job runs, 243,523 instruction commits compared, 110,303 data-memory words, 1,357,215 checks, 0 mismatches. Five independent implementations of the cast (fixed-point model, floating-point reference, base-RV32I kernel, RTL unit, simulator) are required to agree, and the host verifies the round-to-even parity rule against the explicit tie table exhaustively over all 4096 fixed-point values x sticky, plus the register-map fold, before emitting anything. 24 directed data blocks through all four kernels (all zeros, all 1.0, max finite amax, every one of the eight codes, exact ties at all seven midpoints constructed so the shared scale lands on them precisely, the same ties with sticky set, one step below and one step above, negative zeros, subnormals, +Inf, NaN, an all-subnormal block, amax exponents 1 and 2 where the scale clamps at its floor, huge dynamic range, all-negative, alternating signs, every element code 7), 4 multi-block directed jobs, 300 randomised jobs, 33 hand-written ISA conformance results, 7 trap programs one per cause, and directed control-plane tests (CAPS, VERSION, register-map checksum, ten unmapped registers, read-only registers, W1C, interrupt masking with STATUS polling, host memory access ignored while running, soft reset out of a trapped state then a clean job). Mutation-checked with eight injected defects all caught - four numeric (tie parity, sticky dropped, scale off by one binade, amax dropping its accumulator) and four microarchitectural (writeback forward removed, branch shadow not killed, byte-store enable, LB zero-extending). Full differential simulation at IMEM_W x DMEM_W x BLK of 12x12x32, 13x12x32, 12x13x64, 11x11x16 and 12x12x16 - 6,797,115 checks, 0 mismatches. make check regenerates every vector through UBSan + ASan with -fno-sanitize-recover.
projects.summary: Five custom instructions in the execute stage of a three-stage RV32I core, for the MXFP4 cast every quantised-inference deployment runs before a tensor crosses a device boundary. A block of 32 bf16 values becomes one shared E8M0 scale plus 4 bits per element - 4.25 bits/element against bf16's 16 - and the cast that does it is not arithmetic but bit manipulation with a hard rounding rule, which is why a scalar machine needs 46 instructions per element and 1959 per block. MXAMAX folds two elements into a running amax with Inf/NaN clamping and subnormal flushing; MXSCALE derives the shared scale; MXQ4 does the whole quantise including a sticky bit and seven parallel midpoint comparisons a CPU can only do one at a time; MXDQ reconstructs two bf16; MXPK packs. Deliberately not an accelerator behind a bus: an MX cast instruction costs exactly what an ADD costs, so the kernel stays an ordinary loop whose inner iteration is four instructions instead of ninety. Both versions of each kernel - custom-0 and strictly base RV32I - are emitted from the same C file, run on the same core over the same 94 blocks, and are required to leave byte-identical memory, so the speedup is a measured cycle ratio between two programs rather than a comparison against a cost model of a machine nobody built: 11.96x on the quantise, 7.50x on the dequantise, 10.53x on the round trip, 194.4 cycles/block against 2324.5, 0.899 IPC, 1.531 custom instructions per element. The five instructions are about 1010 gate equivalents, 7.8% of the core's logic and a quarter of the base ALU, beside 256 kbit of SRAM. cycles = instructions retired + taken branches + 2 holds exactly on all 780 jobs. 243,523 instruction commits compared against the simulator one at a time, 1,357,215 checks, 0 mismatches; five independent implementations of the cast required to agree, all 65536 bf16 values checked at 11 scales before a vector is written; eight injected defects all caught; 6,797,115 checks across five geometries, 0 mismatches.

projects.name: hid_touch_fusion_engine
projects.domain: sensor fusion / human-interface touch and force sensing
projects.microarchitecture: CORDIC-style iterative shift/subtract coordinate engine: eight parallel baseline clamps feed total/right/bottom reductions, then two parameterized 32-step restoring dividers calculate X and Y concurrently; a threshold bypass returns a neutral centroid without entering the divider path
projects.interface: SPI mode-0 command protocol (CONFIG, FRAME, STATUS, RESULT) over spi_sclk/spi_cs_n/spi_mosi/spi_miso with a separate sticky completion interrupt
projects.software_layer: portable C transport driver for configuration, big-endian frame movement, polling/IRQ completion and result reads; bit-exact reference model, scalar embedded-CPU cost baseline, and deterministic vector generator
projects.verification: Icarus Verilog pin-level SPI differential testbench against the C golden model over 304 frames including zero, baseline, saturated, quadrant and random full-range cases; completion IRQ and result consumption checked; ASan/UBSan vector regeneration clean
projects.summary: SPI-controlled HID sensor-fusion accelerator for two four-quadrant touch/force tiles: hardware clamps calibrated baselines, reduces eight channels into pressure and centroid numerators, and runs two 32-bit restoring dividers concurrently. Measured 33.12-cycle mean launch-to-IRQ latency, 0.03019 non-overlapped frames/clock and 4.47x over the 148-cycle scalar baseline; 304 frames, 0 mismatches.
